title: Nailed the pixel animations I want in my Metroidvania
author: AdamBlue
selftext: Claude had an understanding of the pixel-style character I wanted. Between Grok, Gemini, ChatGPT, and Firefly, I got the look of the character down. Then I generated side-views in Grok. In Firefly, I uploaded the image with animation prompts. After a good 50 or so animation clips, I fed that into Claude which mapped it onto my player character. I feel really good about this.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
That looks extremely clean... 

' After a good 50 or so animation clips, I fed that into Claude which mapped it onto my player character.'

...Yeah, while I am impressed with the results people are getting, it is always the same: brute forcing generations from either image to video tools or interpolation tools, and throwing out most of the work.

That's just too much waste to me.

  
Still waiting on some sort of tool or process that can reliably generate clean sprites / animations without being so incredibly wasteful.

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> brute forcing generations from either image to video tools or interpolation tools, and throwing out most of the work

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body: It's not, and, although I'm fully pro-AI, it's ridiculous the amount of time some people waste prompting when doing is less time intensive. Some people prompt ChatGPT for a HSL change, that's just wasteful or one's usage and time. It's also not how one does art, and on the occasions you do need to brute-force it's just value changes which are still faster.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
i can only speak for myself: 

no, i can't animate things myself. i wish i could. i know for some people it is an enriching process to iterate and learn and get the ball rolling on a cool animation 

for me, i can't. i get defeated instead of inspired. i feel like the thing will never look good and i just give up and be sad about it 

i wish i felt th other way, but my brain doesn't work that way

so these tools have been a godsend for me, and i look forward to when they are a bit better tuned towards animation so they are not as expensive / wasteful (if they ever get there)
